clue.text: Calling campers everywhere, virtually

definitions.meaning: read as a form of address, a call to every camper would be put as one aimed at everybody under canvas
in effect, practically, for all practical purposes

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: an announcement for everyone camping would begin by addressing all who are in tents, which sounds out the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in effect or practically, a synonym of virtually.

clue.text: Asian. giant has' to live in the interior

parts.note: a Titan is a giant of Greek myth
to be is to exist, to live

explanation.surface: A huge Asian creature is obliged to dwell deep inland.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Tibet, in the Himalayas, is an Asian.

clue.text: Leader of pack in Lakeland

indicators.note: says the answer is tucked inside the following word

explanation.surface: Someone guides a group of walkers or hounds in the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: Lakeland is the English Lake District, so a 'pack' there suggests fell hounds or walkers.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Cub Scouts the adult who runs a pack takes the name of the wolf chief from Kipling's Jungle Book.

clue.text: Old queen's.carrier given false directions

a tray is something used to carry food and drinks

explanation.surface: An ancient queen's porter was sent the wrong way.

clue.text: Lancashire town used by wrestlers

definitions.meaning: a mill town in Lancashire, north-west England
a wrestling hold with the arms under the opponent's and the hands locked behind the neck

explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire is a county in north-west England; the town there shares its name with a wrestling hold (full or half).
explanation.definitionFit: The hold and the town share one name, also that of the admiral.

clue.text: Sexy divorce given to quoting

parts.note: a divorcee's former partner is an ex
citing a source means quoting it

explanation.surface: A racy divorce is reported as fond of quotations.

clue.text: Discrimination that always seems to exclude beginners

explanation.surface: Prejudice is the kind of thing that always seems to keep newcomers out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Discrimination' as prejudice against beginners; it is the fine judgement of good style.
explanation.definitionFit: Good judgement in matters of style is called discernment or discrimination.

clue.text: Possible clue for wolf or duck

parts.note: the answer split in two would work as a clue whose solution is wolf: the second word scrambled, with the first as the anagram signal

explanation.surface: Someone muses on how to clue a predator or a waterbird.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as 'wild' plus 'fowl' tells you to rearrange FOWL, which gives WOLF.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducks are typical game birds shot in the wild, an example of the category.

clue.text: Almost 30 seconds inside that's long.

almost the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: thirty written out as a word

explanation.surface: Half a minute spent inside feels like an age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts THIRTY to THIRT; 'inside' puts S into it before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to crave it, as a parched person craves drink.

clue.text: For example, a roll of money

definitions.meaning: a roll is one kind of baked loaf product

explanation.surface: A wad of banknotes is given as an illustration.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll is a baked item of that food, and the word is old slang for cash, like dough.

clue.text: Philosopher speaking to economist and security expert

Adam Smith was the Scottish economist of The Wealth of Nations

explanation.surface: A philosopher chats with an economist and a security consultant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaking' turns LOCKE into its sound-alike LOCKS.

clue.text: Team leader organised a game to delight

parts.note: to run an event is to organise it, past tense ran
a sport is a game

explanation.surface: The team captain set up a match to entertain everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Being carried away with joy is a rapture, as in transports of delight.

clue.text: Ancient tree

definitions.meaning: older, a senior person of the community
a small tree with white flowers and dark berries

explanation.definitionFit: An older person of standing is so named, and so is the shrub that bears berries for wine.

clue.text: Not a line taken by legal official

parts.note: taken as written
RY is short for railway, a railway line

explanation.definitionFit: A notary public is a lawyer who certifies documents, an official of the law.

clue.text: Very attractive person' providing competition

definitions.meaning: a tournament in which losers drop out at each round

clue.text: Express dissatisfaction with policeman wandering 'around without energy

clue.text: Show disapproval about colleague Henry making a lot of fuss

an ally is a partner or associate

explanation.definitionFit: Noisy publicity or uproar is a great deal of hullabaloo.

clue.text: Cricketer from Derby in a state?

definitions.meaning: a player who delivers the ball in cricket
in American states a derby is the domed felt hat

explanation.surface: A cricket player from Derby is getting worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby is an English county town, but here it is the American name for the hard round hat; 'in a state' means in a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket player who delivers the ball shares a name with the British hard felt hat Americans call a derby.

clue.text: A beastly director e'er lacking charm

clue.text: Trainer bringing monarch inside the ground
